duplicate_polarised_10k_archive_relation.note: The two archives retain different serialized bytes but decode to the same complete result object.

limitations: Exact intervals apply to the separately normalized serialized policy in the configured binary64 terminal model. They do not certify the raw unnormalized float profile, an equilibrium for the weighted raised game, or unrestricted Hold'em.

methodology.archive_identity: The duplicate matrix-free polarised 10k result remains two source-report rows: distinct raw serialized bytes, equal decoded complete payloads.
methodology.exact_model: Existing turn_rational_certificate helper; complete river trees have no chance nodes; default chance grouping remains scan.
methodology.independent_replay: Original turn_river_validation replay and compare_result run before exact arithmetic for every pinned policy.
methodology.normalization: Each serialized binary64 action probability is converted with Fraction.from_float and each row is exactly normalized; original float inputs and raw policy files are never mutated.
methodology.polarised_crosscheck: All eight Fraction metrics are compared exactly with the separate river_analytical five-history, 16/4 legal pure-response witness; each interval must contain value 25.
methodology.provenance: Parent canonical reports, the approved hardened-replay bridge, and all fifteen raw policy SHA-256 values are pinned. The bridge binds the earlier extension report to the hardened whole-file validator and its exact twelve policy identities. Other historical checks cover only actual numeric-model dependencies with path/line-ending normalization; current-run source fingerprints are strict raw hashes before and after.
methodology.resource_scope: Unchanged helper limits: 100,000 logical work units, depth 64, and 65,536 Fraction bits. These are audit work/operand limits, not CPU, memory, or RSS bounds.
methodology.weighted_scope: The weighted raised fixture receives exact profile EV and legal own-information BR bounds only; no known equilibrium value is asserted.
